title: Smoothness at a prime descends along a field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $K$ a field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension] and $S$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $S_K=K\otimes_kS$, a $K$-algebra through $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes1$, with the ring map $j:S\to S_K$, $s\mapsto1\otimes s$. Let $\mathfrak q_K\subset S_K$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak q=j^{-1}(\mathfrak q_K)$, a prime ideal of $S$. If $K\to S_K$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q_K$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] (there is $h\in S_K\setminus\mathfrak q_K$ with $(S_K)_h$ a smooth $K$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]), then $k\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$: there is $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $S_g$ a smooth $k$-algebra.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 02UQ (lemma-smooth-field-change-local, line 37747), the implication 'S_K smooth at q_K => S smooth at q'; its proof (line 37756) is 'a special case of' Lemma Tag 00TG (lemma-flat-base-change-locus-smooth, line 37713) with R = k, R' = K (flat over the field k); tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (02UQ,algebra-lemma-smooth-field-change-local; 00TG,algebra-lemma-flat-base-change-locus-smooth)

proof.text: (Finite presentation and the local flat map.) A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field), so the finite type $k$-algebra $S$ is finitely presented [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. The tensor symmetry $S\otimes_kK\cong K\otimes_kS$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes s$, carries $s\mapsto s\otimes1$ to $j:s\mapsto1\otimes s$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] with $D=S$ makes $j:S\to S_K$ faithfully flat; by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] the induced $j_{\mathfrak q_K}:S_{\mathfrak q}\to(S_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ is a flat local map, and by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] it is faithfully flat. The same field-flatness fact with $D=k$ makes $k\to K$ flat. Base change of a finite presentation gives a finite presentation of $S_K$ over $K$ [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change], using the same tensor symmetry.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 02UQ (lemma-smooth-field-change-local), reduction to Lemma Tag 00TG (lemma-flat-base-change-locus-smooth), hypotheses of 00TG; Lemmas 00FP, 00HT and 00HR

proof.text: (Smoothness upstairs gives local cotangent conditions.) Choose $h\in S_K\setminus\mathfrak q_K$ with $(S_K)_h$ smooth over $K$ by [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. Its naive cotangent homology is zero and its Kähler differentials form a finite projective module by [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Localize this smooth algebra further at the prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q_K$: [lem-weil-pbc-h1-cotangent-localization] identifies $H_1(L_{S_K/K})_{\mathfrak q_K}$ with the localization of $H_1(L_{(S_K)_h/K})=0$, and [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] identifies $(\Omega_{S_K/K})_{\mathfrak q_K}$ with the localization of $\Omega_{(S_K)_h/K}$. The latter is finite free over the local ring $(S_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free] (localizing its free neighbourhood further at $\mathfrak q_K$).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TG (lemma-flat-base-change-locus-smooth), lines 37731-37739: the vanishing of H_1 and projectivity of differentials upstairs; Lemma Tag 07BU (lemma-smooth-at-point), implication (1) to (2)

proof.text: (Compare the two cotangent modules.) Put $B=S_K$, $p=\mathfrak q$, $Q=\mathfrak q_K$, $U=S\setminus p$ and $T=B\setminus Q$, so $j(U)\subseteq T$ by $p=j^{-1}(Q)$. Since $k\to K$ is flat (step 1), [lem-weil-pbc-h1-cotangent-flat-base-change] gives $B\otimes_SH_1(L_{S/k})\cong H_1(L_{B/K})$, and [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] gives $B\otimes_S\Omega_{S/k}\cong\Omega_{B/K}$. For either $S$-module $M=H_1(L_{S/k})$ or $M=\Omega_{S/k}$, first localize $B\otimes_SM$ at $Q$: [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with $R=S$, $A=B$, its $A$-module equal to $B$, its $R$-module equal to $M$, and its multiplicative set equal to $T$ gives $(B\otimes_SM)_Q\cong B_Q\otimes_SM$, $(b\otimes m)/t\mapsto(b/t)\otimes m$. Equivalently this is $B_Q\otimes_B(B\otimes_SM)\cong B_Q\otimes_SM$ by localization of a module and tensor associativity. Next [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] with base ring $S$ and set $U$ applies to $B_Q$ and $M$: $j(U)$ consists of units in $B_Q$, so $B_Q\to B_Q$ is its own $U$-localization, while $M\to M_p$ is the other $U$-localization. That node says $B_Q\otimes_SM\to B_Q\otimes_{S_p}M_p$ is a $U$-localization; its source is already $U$-local, so it is an isomorphism, explicitly $b\otimes m\mapsto b\otimes(m/1)$ with inverse $b\otimes(m/s)\mapsto b/j(s)\otimes m$. Thus $(B\otimes_SM)_Q\cong B_Q\otimes_{S_p}M_p$ for each of the two named modules. Localizing the two displayed base-change isomorphisms therefore gives $B_Q\otimes_{S_p}H_1(L_{S/k})_p\cong H_1(L_{B/K})_Q=0$ and $B_Q\otimes_{S_p}(\Omega_{S/k})_p\cong(\Omega_{B/K})_Q$, which is finite free, hence finite projective, by step 2.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TG (lemma-flat-base-change-locus-smooth), first and second paragraphs: Lemma 00S4 (lemma-change-base-NL) and localization of its H_1 and Omega comparisons

proof.text: (Descend the two conditions.) Since $S_{\mathfrak q}\to(S_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ is faithfully flat (step 1), the zero tensor product in step 3 forces $H_1(L_{S/k})_{\mathfrak q}=0$: apply exactness reflection in [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] to $0\to H_1(L_{S/k})_{\mathfrak q}\to0$. The $S_{\mathfrak q}$-module $(\Omega_{S/k})_{\mathfrak q}$ is finite: choose finitely many algebra generators of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], present it as a quotient of $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, and use the surjection $S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/k}\twoheadrightarrow\Omega_{S/k}$ from [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-first-exact-sequence] (the quotient has $\Omega_{S/P}=0$); [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis] makes the source free of rank $n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-descends-flat-local], this finite module is projective over $S_{\mathfrak q}$ because its tensor extension is finite projective by step 3; over the local ring $S_{\mathfrak q}$ it is finite free, as the same node states.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TG (lemma-flat-base-change-locus-smooth), lines 37734-37743: faithful-flat descent of H_1 vanishing and Lemma Tag 00O1 for finite projectivity of Omega; finite generation follows from Lemmas 00RS and 00RX

proof.text: (Conclude at the contracted prime.) The map $k\to S$ is finitely presented (step 1), $H_1(L_{S/k})_{\mathfrak q}=0$ and $(\Omega_{S/k})_{\mathfrak q}$ is finite free (step 4). Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-naive-cotangent-criterion] gives $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $S_g$ smooth over $k$, exactly the conclusion of [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].
